source.title: Trainability, Expressivity and Interpretability in Gated Neural ODEs
source.authors: T. Kim; T. Can; K. Krishnamurthy

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper and appendices; no cutoff or garbling is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares initialization schemes and reports task performance for neural ODE models, bearing conceptually on initialization and trainability. It does not reproduce the claim’s CIFAR classification experiments or measure training classification error.
record.gate_note: The study reports initialization comparisons in speech-command classification and, for gnODE, character classification and Walker2D prediction. Its other results on flip-flop tasks, trajectory fitting and real-world tasks do not test the listed claim versions. No results cited from other work are recorded as this study’s own.
record.test_reason: The study compares neural ODE initialization recipes using final test accuracy and test MSE. These measures do not test V4's learning-speed or trainable-depth effects in plain networks. Its dynamical-stability theory also does not establish those training effects. No own results test V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' narrow initialization conclusion: they report some evidence of improved performance when critical initialization is paired with a tanh final nonlinearity. This does not isolate initialization's contribution. Their broader conclusion emphasizes gating's benefits for task performance, continuous-attractor learning and interpretable dynamics in low-dimensional gnODEs.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains gated and ungated neural ODEs on time-series tasks, rather than large convolutional classifiers on CIFAR benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization comparisons vary by task: critical initialization improves the reported speech-command and some character-classification accuracies, matches the noncritical result for 70% dropped character data, and gives worse Walker2D test MSE. The authors also state that tanh as the final nonlinearity is important for the critical initialization comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: Critical-initialization recipes yield higher SpeechCommands test accuracy and slightly higher CharacterTrajectories accuracy at 30% and 50% dropping; accuracy is equal at displayed precision at 70% dropping. Appendix H.1 couples critical initialization with tanh and standard initialization with an identity final activation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization-and-activation recipes can affect final neural ODE test accuracy, with task-dependent benefits.

fits_no_version.finding: Walker2D test MSE is 0.588 ± 0.003 for the critical recipe versus 0.552 ± 0.019 for the noncritical recipe, following hyperparameter search.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The critical neural ODE recipe does not uniformly improve final test performance across tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix A derives initialization-dependent dynamical stability and criticality for neural ODEs, including instability without a leak term except at zero initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neural ODE initialization and architecture determine initial dynamical stability.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning; PMLR 202, 2023
record.problems: The initialization comparisons report test task performance, not training classification error, training speed, or maximum trainable depth. The initialization comparison in Table 3 does not identify which of Glorot normal or Kaiming normal produced the noncritical result.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant initialization-comparison results were left out.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels and recipe-dependent exceptions.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training degradation in plain convolutional networks, identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization exceptions.
Initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth in plain networks, including orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and very deep convolutional networks.
Loss recovery, curvature changes, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Batch normalization effects on training speed and tolerated learning rates, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The numerical comparisons do not justify the record's V4 verdicts. Unmeasured learning speed and trainable depth are untested, rather than scope limitations or failures. The reported comparisons follow hyperparameter searches and are not established as otherwise identical initialization ablations.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and training classification error are not tested.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks, spurious minima and width comparisons are not tested.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks, depth effects and normalization are not tested.

The study does not measure learning speed, maximum trainable depth, or vanishing/exploding signals and gradients. Its initialization comparisons use neural ODE models and task performance rather than the plain feedforward networks named in the version.
Learning rates above a stability limit, curvature, sharpness and divergence are not tested.
Batch normalization, its learning-speed or learning-rate effects, and Fixup are not tested.
